significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that ESM-2 features for hydrophobic packing, salt bridges, and disulfide bonding "drop specifically for mechanism-breaking mutations" and vary monotonically with hydrophobicity change or Coulombic energy while remaining comparatively stable under mechanism-preserving substitutions. This establishes a physics-linked representational phenomenon and a constrained account of what those internal features track—not a causal mechanism for model outputs—and fixes expectations across mutation strengths rather than merely asserting annotation decodability; that distinction matters for interpreting the kinds of biological-concept features reported by InterPLM and related protein-model probing work. Verified false and verified true are distinguishable, and the negative branch would show that these candidate features fail the stated physics-grounded criterion, although it would not prove that all representations in the model are "merely correlational." In the topic-substitution check, the generic question of whether scientific-model representations correspond to mechanisms would not earn this score; the claim-specific counterfactual selectivity plus quantitative dose-response law places it above the obvious annotation-probing hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "mechanism-selectivity index" and the claimed "monotone dose-response" between feature activation and physical quantities; these provide a concrete audit of whether a recovered feature deserves a mechanistic interpretation. The audit can gate trust before a feature is used in protein design or variant-effect workflows, but relative to an individual biological failure it is principally a post-hoc or pre-deployment validation tool rather than a predictor that forecasts which future variants will fail. After feature re-extraction on another architecture, the conclusion does not specify what value or even direction must be recovered, because its substantive scope is ESM-2 and three selected mechanisms, so another model must largely be tested afresh rather than merely recalibrated. The downstream users include protein-model auditors and practitioners applying the stated rule to use features "only with external biophysical validation," but the topic-substitution check shows that this usable metric—not biology's general importance—supports the score, while its model-family and mechanism scope keeps it below broad-transfer reach.
